detailed_rationale:
Black Box is an Essar-Group-promoted (~70% holding) global ICT infrastructure and network-integration solutions provider operating across the Americas, APAC, and EMEA. The quality metrics here are genuinely strong -- ROE 26.8% (35.2% on a 3-year average) and ROCE 22.2%, well above most names in this batch -- and FY26 results were solid in isolation (Rs.6,322 Cr sales, Rs.218 Cr net profit, +6% YoY, with operating margin improved to ~9% from a historical 4-6%). The problem is the growth base this sits on: 3-year revenue CAGR is just 0.18%, essentially flat, and the FY26 uptick is the first real growth in several years rather than a continuation of an established trend.

The valuation has run well ahead of that flat-growth history: P/E is now 48.9-68.7x (our CSV's higher figure likely reflects a slightly earlier price pull than Screener's live figure; using the better live number per standard practice, ~49x is still rich for a business with a 3-year growth CAGR near zero). Working capital has also deteriorated (debtor days 35 to 67), a real, measurable cash-conversion concern rather than a cosmetic one. The FY26 margin improvement and modest revenue pickup are genuine positives, but one year of a 6% uptick after three years of stagnation is not yet strong enough evidence of a durable growth reacceleration to underwrite the current multiple.

Reverse-DCF: to justify ~49-69x earnings, the market needs Black Box to sustain double-digit growth for several years; the demonstrated history (flat for three years, one recent uptick) does not yet support that expectation, even though the underlying returns on capital (ROE/ROCE) are genuinely excellent. This reads as a high-quality business priced for a growth inflection that has one data point of evidence, not several.
recommendation_rationale: We are not rescuing this to Hold despite genuinely strong ROE/ROCE, because the growth problem is real and structural (three years of essentially flat revenue), not a scoring artifact, and the valuation has re-rated well ahead of any confirmed growth inflection. Combined with deteriorating working capital, the quant Sell is the more defensible call until at least a second consecutive quarter or year of the FY26 growth pickup is confirmed.
summary: Black Box is an Essar-Group-owned global ICT infrastructure and network-integration provider with genuinely strong returns on capital (ROE ~27%, ROCE ~22%). However, revenue was essentially flat over the prior three years before a modest 6% pickup in FY26, and the stock now trades at roughly 49-69 times earnings -- a valuation that requires sustained double-digit growth the company has not yet demonstrated. Working capital has also worsened. We rate this a Sell on valuation grounds relative to the still-unproven growth reacceleration.
positive_para: Best-in-class capital efficiency for this batch (ROE ~27%, ROCE ~22%), a first real growth uptick in FY26 (+6% revenue, margin improving to ~9% from a historical 4-6%), and a large, stable promoter base (Essar Group, ~70%).
negative_para: Three-year revenue CAGR is essentially zero (0.18%), meaning the FY26 uptick is a single data point, not a demonstrated trend, and the stock's valuation (~49-69x earnings) already prices a sustained double-digit growth reacceleration that has not yet been confirmed over multiple periods. Debtor days worsened from 35 to 67, a real cash-conversion deterioration.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~49-69x multiple requires several years of sustained double-digit growth; against a three-year revenue CAGR of essentially zero and only one recent quarter/year of pickup, the price is ahead of the evidence, notwithstanding genuinely strong ROE/ROCE.
